purpose: The labelled set behind the §13 row 21 entity-fence audit. It exists because the 26 August reading was measured against six plants defined inline in a shell heredoc that was never committed, so the figure it produced could not be reproduced from the tree and could not be checked. Nothing here is evidentiary; the trace harness stamps every row it writes NON_EVIDENTIARY and refuses to register or admit.
labels: is_class_level is the independent label, applied against §3.7's own definition: a mechanism names a regularity, an episode names an entity bound to a time. The fence's verdict is compared against it. The two arms are not the same kind of thing and are not reported as one. The 36 class-level subjects were DRAWN, by agent sweep, so the share of them the fence refuses is a rate. The 6 subjects labelled is_class_level=false are AUTHORED PROBES, one per named route into the fence, so what they yield is coverage of those routes and never a rate: a chosen set has no sampling frame, and a proportion over one estimates nothing.
labeller: model_clerk. Classification against a fixed definition is clerk work, but row 21 specifies HAND labels and 200 of them. These are neither. Operator ratification is outstanding and the reading is provisional until it lands.
probes: The six are authored probes rather than drawn episodes, and the term 'episode-level' is not used of them anywhere: it would imply a sample of episode-level material, which they are not. The originals are lost, and rather than reconstruct them from a report that recorded only their count, each probes one route into the fence, named in probe_route. One route is deliberately left open: plant-03 is an expected pass, and a probe set that cannot fail measures nothing.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: Clusters of on-market acquisitions by two or more directors of the same listed entity, each separately disclosed on an Appendix 3Y with 'nature of change' recorded as an on-market trade and with dates of change falling close together.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on ASX-listed operating entities across the full capitalisation range, restricted to ordinary fully paid securities and excluding externally managed listed investment companies, stapled trusts and entities whose only director filings arise from scheme or option vesting.
proposal.mechanism_note: The Appendix 3Y is a per-director form carrying date of change, direct/indirect interest, number acquired, number disposed, holdings before and after, and an explicit 'nature of change' field, so on-market purchases are separable from allocations, vestings and off-market transfers. Because each director lodges individually and the entity lodges to the announcements platform, simultaneous board-level activity appears as several structurally identical filings against one entity rather than as a single aggregate disclosure.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: Director or key-management acquisitions that the Appendix 3Y itself flags as having occurred inside a closed period, together with the recorded answer to whether prior written clearance was given and the date of that clearance.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on ASX-listed entities of any capitalisation that are subject to Listing Rule 12.9 and have lodged a trading policy, excluding foreign-exempt listings and entities admitted under a category where the trading policy requirement does not bite.
proposal.mechanism_note: Listing Rules 12.9-12.12 force every entity to define at least one fixed closed period, to lodge its trading policy on admission and to re-lodge material changes within five business days, and the policy is released through the Market Announcements Platform. Part 3 of the Appendix 3Y then asks directly whether the interests were traded during a closed period and whether written clearance preceded the trade.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: A director's transition from a nil registered holding to a non-nil direct holding acquired on market, identifiable from the 'no. of securities held prior to change' field reading nil against a non-zero number acquired.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on ASX-listed entities across small, mid and large capitalisation bands, filtered to directors whose first non-nil holding is acquired rather than issued, and excluding initial holdings arising from admission, IPO subscription or contractual appointment arrangements.
proposal.mechanism_note: Guidance Note 22 requires notification of securities registered in the director's name and of securities in which the director holds a relevant interest, with the notice due within five business days of the change and the director expected to inform the entity within three. Because the form demands the holding both before and after, the boundary case of a first acquisition is directly readable from the disclosure without inference.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: Substantial holder crossings in which a person and their associates first come to hold relevant interests in voting shares at or above the statutory five per cent level, disclosed on a Form 603 notice of initial substantial holder.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on ASX-quoted voting share classes across the full capitalisation range, restricted to notices lodged by institutional or corporate holders rather than by the entity's own related parties, and excluding crossings that arise mechanically from a reduction in the number of shares on issue.
proposal.mechanism_note: Section 671B and Regulatory Guide 5 make the five per cent crossing itself the trigger for disclosure, and the notice must set out the relevant interest, its nature and the associates aggregated into it. Relevant interest is defined broadly enough to capture indirect, implied or informal control over voting or disposal.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: Movements in an existing substantial holding of at least the statutory one per cent, disclosed on a Form 604 notice of change of interests of substantial holder, distinguished by the stated nature of the change.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on ASX-quoted voting shares across mid and large capitalisation bands where multiple substantial holders coexist, filtered to changes in beneficial economic exposure and excluding changes recorded as intra-group transfers between wholly owned members of the same corporate group.
proposal.mechanism_note: Once a person is a substantial holder, every movement of at least one per cent must be notified, which converts an ongoing position into a series of dated, itemised disclosures rather than a single snapshot. Regulatory Guide 5 also carves out certain intra-group transfers under s610(3A) so that internal restructures do not present as genuine accumulation.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: Substantial holding changes whose stated basis is a securities lending or borrowing arrangement, or an equity derivative or relevant agreement conferring disposal rights, rather than an outright purchase or sale of shares.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on ASX-quoted voting shares of entities large and liquid enough to support a stock lending market, filtered to notices where the disclosed nature of the relevant interest names a lending arrangement, a derivative, or an agreement giving control of voting or disposal.
proposal.mechanism_note: Regulatory Guide 5 treats lending and derivative arrangements explicitly: relief instrument 2021/821 modifies s608(8) so a lender's relevant interest in loaned securities survives the borrower ceasing to hold one, and agreements conferring disposal rights, including derivative agreements, can create relevant interests and associations.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: Announcement of a new on-market buy-back by a listed entity via an Appendix 3C notification, including whether the programme sits within the 10/12 limit and therefore proceeds without a security holder resolution.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on ASX-listed entities across the full capitalisation range, restricted to buy-backs of quoted ordinary securities and excluding minimum-holding buy-backs, employee share scheme buy-backs and selective buy-backs from identified holders.
proposal.mechanism_note: The Appendix 3C separates on-market, equal access, selective, employee scheme and other buy-backs on the face of the form, records the total securities on issue in the class and the maximum number proposed to be bought back, and caps the programme's end date at twelve months.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: The daily notification stream generated by an active on-market buy-back, in which the entity must notify the market of each day's purchases before trading recommences, and the pattern of days on which the entity does or does not appear in that stream.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on ASX-listed entities with a live on-market buy-back programme, across mid and large capitalisation bands where programmes typically run for extended periods, and excluding equal access and selective structures whose final notification obligations run on a different clock.
proposal.mechanism_note: Part 4 of the Appendix 3C regime requires daily notification at least half an hour before trading commences on the day following any day on which securities were bought back, and final notification is due the same business day for on-market programmes. That cadence turns execution into a dated public series rather than a single retrospective total.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: Scheduled periodic results disclosures lodged with ASX Market Announcements, comprising the Appendix 4D half-year report and the Appendix 4E preliminary final report, each opening with the prescribed 'results for announcement to market' block.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on ASX-listed entities with ordinary reporting calendars across all capitalisation bands, excluding entities whose primary periodic obligation is a quarterly Appendix 4C cash flow report or a mining and oil and gas activities report, and excluding trusts reporting monthly net tangible asset backing only.
proposal.mechanism_note: Chapter 4 fixes both the content and the outer deadline: two months after period end for the half-year and preliminary final reports, three months for the annual report, with a longer allowance for exploration entities, all lodged with the market announcements office.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: Additions to and deletions from S&P/ASX index families at a scheduled review, announced ahead of the rebalance taking effect and distributed to the market through the ASX announcements platform.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on the ASX-quoted universe eligible for the headline S&P/ASX index families, spanning the capitalisation bands those indices cover, filtered to scheduled review changes and excluding intra-review replacements caused by corporate actions such as mergers or delistings.
proposal.mechanism_note: Membership is governed by a published methodology with a fixed calendar, quarterly reviews for the flagship index, semi-annual for the broader ones, and by stated eligibility inputs: float-adjusted market capitalisation over a defined lookback, an investable weight factor floor, and a relative liquidity measure. Ranking buffers around the entry and exit positions damp churn.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: Publication of aggregate short position totals per financial product in the ASIC short position reports, and changes in those totals across consecutive reporting days.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on ASX-quoted products that fall within the short position reporting regime, across the full capitalisation range, filtered to products with continuous reporting coverage and excluding products where reporting coverage begins or ends part-way through the observation window.
proposal.mechanism_note: Short sellers report positions directly or through an authorised submitting entity via FIX position report messages, and ASIC publishes the total of short positions for each product for a given reporting day at T+4 with all short seller identifying information stripped. That produces a regular, product-level, de-identified public series with a known and constant publication lag.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: Life sciences disclosure milestones announced under continuous disclosure, comprising clinical trial initiation and results announcements, regulatory submission and approval steps, and reimbursement decisions such as a Pharmaceutical Benefits Advisory Committee recommendation to list or not list a product.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on ASX-listed life sciences and healthcare entities, weighted toward the small and mid capitalisation bands where a single product programme dominates the entity, and excluding diversified healthcare operators and service providers with no clinical development or reimbursement pipeline.
proposal.mechanism_note: The ASX code asks life sciences entities to announce trials with endpoints, blinding, subject numbers, control arm, selection criteria and expected duration at initiation, to report progress without creating a misleading impression, and to report outcomes whether favourable or not. It treats PBAC listing recommendations and other payer approvals as material.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: An insider files a SEDI insider report disclosing an open-market acquisition of the issuer's equity made at the insider's own discretion, as distinguished from an acquisition reported under the automatic securities purchase plan alternative reporting route.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on TSX-listed non-investment-fund operating issuers across the full capitalisation range from small through large cap, restricted to common equity classes with continuous SEDI coverage, and excluding issuers listed only on TSX Venture.
proposal.mechanism_note: NI 55-104 splits insider acquisitions into two reporting channels. Discretionary changes in beneficial ownership must be filed within five days of the change, while acquisitions under an automatic securities purchase plan qualify for alternative reporting, disclosable annually by March 31 or in acceptable summary form with a December 31 deemed transaction date.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: An insider files paired SEDI reports on the exercise of a convertible security, one recording the disposition or reduction of the option, warrant or right and a second recording the acquisition of the underlying common shares under the corresponding nature-of-transaction code.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on TSX-listed issuers with equity-settled compensation arrangements, across mid and large capitalisation, restricted to reporting insiders who are directors or officers of the issuer rather than of a significant shareholder or major subsidiary.
proposal.mechanism_note: SEDI requires an insider exercising options or warrants to report the acquisition of the resulting common shares using transaction code 51, 54 or 57 as appropriate, and NI 55-104 requires separate insider reports within five days covering both the change in the convertible instrument and the change in the underlying security holdings.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: A reporting insider files a SEDI report for an equity monetization transaction such as a prepaid forward, a costless collar or a total return swap, which alters the insider's economic exposure to the issuer's shares while leaving registered ownership of those shares unchanged.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on TSX-listed issuers where control-block or founder holders are present, across mid and large capitalisation, restricted to common equity and to insiders who are significant shareholders or executive officers.
proposal.mechanism_note: CSA Staff Notice 55-312 sets out that derivative-based arrangements letting an investor receive a cash amount similar to proceeds of disposition while retaining legal ownership are reportable, with forwards filed as acquisitions of third-party derivatives under nature-of-transaction code 70, collars filed as separate put and call legs, and total return swaps filed as equity swaps.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: An acquiror crosses the ten percent ownership-or-control threshold in a class of voting or equity securities of a reporting issuer and discharges the early warning obligation by issuing a news release before the opening of trading on the next business day and filing an early warning report within two business days.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on Canadian reporting issuers listed on TSX, across small through large capitalisation, restricted to classes of voting or equity securities and excluding acquirors filing under the alternative monthly reporting exemption.
proposal.mechanism_note: The early warning system fixes both the trigger and the clock. The threshold is ten percent of the outstanding securities of the class, tightening to five percent while a take-over bid is outstanding, and the news release must precede the next trading session with the report following within two business days.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: An acquiror already subject to early warning reporting files a further report on an increase or decrease of two percent or more in its holdings of the class, or on a material change to the facts previously disclosed in its early warning report.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on TSX-listed Canadian reporting issuers across the full capitalisation range, restricted to acquirors already above the initial early warning threshold in the same class of securities, and excluding eligible institutional investors reporting monthly.
proposal.mechanism_note: Once the initial threshold is crossed, the regime requires a fresh report for every increase or decrease of two percent or more in holdings, and also on a material change in the previously disclosed facts, including the acquiror's stated plans or intentions.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: An eligible institutional investor without a control intention crosses one of the alternative monthly reporting thresholds and files a report within ten days of the end of the month in which the crossing occurred, in place of the immediate news release and early warning report.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on TSX-listed Canadian reporting issuers across mid and large capitalisation, restricted to filings by financial institutions, pension funds and registered investment managers electing the alternative monthly reporting exemption.
proposal.mechanism_note: NI 62-103 gives eligible institutional investors a separate reporting lane keyed to month end, with reports due within ten days of the end of the month at the ten, twelve and a half, fifteen and seventeen and a half percent thresholds, available only to holders that do not have the intention to make a take-over bid or to change control.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: A TSX-listed issuer files a Form 12 Notice of Intention to Make a Normal Course Issuer Bid together with the accompanying press release, establishing an authorised repurchase capacity and a bid period before any purchases occur.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on TSX-listed non-investment-fund issuers across small through large capitalisation, restricted to bids in listed common equity classes and excluding substantial issuer bids and formal issuer bids made by circular.
proposal.mechanism_note: The TSX requires acceptance of a Form 12 notice and a press release before an NCIB begins, and the notice states the class, the number of securities sought and the bid duration. The authorised capacity is bounded by the greater of ten percent of the public float on the acceptance date and five percent of the outstanding securities of the class.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: A TSX-listed issuer conducting a normal course issuer bid files its monthly purchase report within ten days of the end of each month in which purchases were made, disclosing the number of securities acquired and their disposition.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on TSX-listed non-investment-fund issuers with an accepted normal course issuer bid outstanding, across the full capitalisation range, restricted to listed common equity classes.
proposal.mechanism_note: Monthly reporting turns an authorisation into an execution record. Because daily purchases by non-investment-fund issuers are capped at the greater of twenty-five percent of average daily trading volume in the class and one thousand securities, with a separate block purchase exception, the monthly filings show utilisation against a capacity that the exchange rules already bound.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: A TSX-listed issuer submits an automatic share purchase plan to the exchange for review, delegating repurchase execution to a broker under pre-set instructions so that buying may continue through periods when the issuer itself would be restricted from trading.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on TSX-listed non-investment-fund issuers running a normal course issuer bid, across mid and large capitalisation, restricted to issuers with scheduled financial reporting blackout windows.
proposal.mechanism_note: An automatic share purchase plan is an agreement with a broker that conducts the purchases, and a draft must be submitted to the TSX for review before implementation. This creates a disclosed distinction between repurchases executed under standing pre-cleared instructions and repurchases the issuer directs contemporaneously.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: Participants and access persons calculate and file aggregate short positions in each listed and quoted security as of the fifteenth day and the last day of each calendar month, producing a twice-monthly consolidated short position record.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on securities listed on Canadian marketplaces under CIRO market surveillance, across small through large capitalisation, restricted to listed and quoted equity securities and excluding debt instruments.
proposal.mechanism_note: UMIR 10.10 fixes both the calculation dates and the filing lag: positions are struck as of the fifteenth and the last day of each calendar month and filed not later than two trading days after the calculation date. Positions are aggregated by individual account and by security.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: A TSX-listed issuer files its Form 1 report of changes in issued and outstanding securities within ten days after the end of a month in which the share count changed, or files a nil report where no change occurred.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on TSX-listed issuers whose share count feeds public float determinations, across mid and large capitalisation, restricted to listed equity classes and excluding structured products and non-corporate issuers.
proposal.mechanism_note: Issued and outstanding share counts are the input that float-weighted index maintenance consumes, and the TSX supplies that input on a fixed monthly cadence through Form 1 filed via TMX LINX, with quarterly nil reports when nothing changed. Related capital events arrive through their own channels on their own clocks.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: A TSX-listed issuer disseminates a scheduled financial results announcement through a recognised newswire service, having operated a designated pre-announcement trading blackout for insiders that opens into a trading window after the release.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Intended to hold on TSX-listed non-investment-fund reporting issuers with regular quarterly and annual reporting cycles, across mid and large capitalisation, restricted to issuers with a published insider trading policy defining blackout windows.
proposal.mechanism_note: TSX timely disclosure guidance directs that material information be disclosed forthwith once known to management, that Market Surveillance be pre-notified for announcements made during trading hours, and that dissemination run through a recognised newswire reaching the national financial press and all participating organisations.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: Managers' transactions notified after the expiry of a closed period, where a single notification aggregates several executions carried out on the same day.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Regulated-market equity listings on Frankfurt (Prime Standard) and Euronext Amsterdam/Paris/Brussels, large- and mid-cap segment bands, restricted to issuers with ordinary shares as the notified instrument and excluding collective investment undertakings and debt-only issuers.
proposal.mechanism_note: Article 19(1) obliges persons discharging managerial responsibilities and persons closely associated to notify the issuer and the competent authority promptly after the transaction date, and Article 19(11) closes a window ahead of interim and year-end reports. The notification form carries a transaction date, a place of execution and a volume, and permits several executions of the same nature on the same day to be reported in one line.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: Managers' transactions executed inside a closed period under an issuer-granted permission, typically the exercise of options or warrants expiring within the window or a pre-committed employee scheme instruction.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Continental European regulated markets under BaFin and AFM supervision, large-cap through small-cap bands, restricted to issuers operating share-based remuneration schemes and excluding funds and investment vehicles.
proposal.mechanism_note: Articles 7 to 9 of Delegated Regulation 2016/522 set out when an issuer may allow a manager to trade during a closed period: exceptional circumstances that are urgent, unforeseen, compelling and external, or an enumerated category of transaction such as employee share schemes with no timing discretion, options or warrants expiring in the window, savings schemes entered into beforehand, transfers between the manager's own accounts, and statutorily required acquisitions.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: Managers' transaction notifications whose reported transaction type is the pledging or lending of the issuer's own financial instruments rather than an acquisition or disposal.
proposal.measured_on_intention: German and Dutch regulated-market listings, mid- and small-cap bands, restricted to issuers with an identifiable founder, family or concentrated managerial shareholding and excluding state-controlled entities.
proposal.mechanism_note: Article 19(7) MAR and Article 10 of Delegated Regulation 2016/522 place pledging and lending inside the notifiable set, alongside acquisitions, disposals, option exercises, equity swaps, conversions, gifts and inheritances, and require the nature of the transaction to be stated.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: Managers' transaction notifications filed by a person closely associated with a manager while the issuer's closed period is running, given that the closed-period prohibition binds the manager but the notification duty extends further.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Regulated-market listings in Germany and the Netherlands, full capitalisation range from large through small cap, restricted to issuers where closely associated persons (spouses, dependants, controlled legal persons, trusts) appear in the notification history.
proposal.mechanism_note: ESMA's MAR Q&A on managers' transactions states that the transaction types caught by the closed-period prohibition in Article 19(11) match those notifiable under Article 19(1), but that Article 19(11) applies only where the manager transacts on own account or for a third party, while Article 19(1) also reaches persons closely associated.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: Major holdings notifications where a notification threshold is crossed because the issuer's total number of voting rights changed rather than because the holder traded.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Issuers on Euronext Amsterdam and the Frankfurt regulated market, mid- and small-cap bands, restricted to issuers with active capital-structure activity (capital increases, conversions, cancellations) and excluding closed-end funds.
proposal.mechanism_note: Articles 9 and 12 of the Transparency Directive attach the notification duty to reaching, exceeding or falling below a set percentage of voting rights, and require the holder to notify promptly after becoming aware of the crossing, with the issuer then publishing. Because the percentage is a ratio against the issuer's total voting rights, and the issuer separately publishes changes to that denominator, the disclosure record distinguishes passive crossings from crossings driven by acquisition.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: Major holdings notifications where the crossing is attributable to financial instruments with similar economic effect, counted on a delta-adjusted basis, rather than to directly held shares or voting rights.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Continental European regulated markets under AFM and BaFin oversight, large- and mid-cap bands, restricted to issuers with liquid single-stock derivatives and excluding issuers whose notifications come solely from index-tracking custodians.
proposal.mechanism_note: Article 13 extends notification to holders of financial instruments giving a right to acquire shares and to instruments with similar economic effect whether or not settled physically, and Article 13a requires aggregation of shares, instruments conferring entitlement and similar-effect instruments; for cash-settled instruments the number of voting rights is computed on a delta-adjusted basis.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: Aggregated public disclosure of buy-back programme executions made at the far end of the permitted reporting window rather than promptly after execution.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Euronext and Deutsche Boerse regulated-market listings running an announced buy-back under the MAR safe harbour, large- and mid-cap bands, restricted to open-market repurchases and excluding tender offers, reverse auctions and stabilisation.
proposal.mechanism_note: Article 2 of Delegated Regulation 2016/1052 requires disclosure of the programme's purpose, monetary allocation, maximum number of shares and duration before trading begins, then reporting of transactions to the competent authority and public disclosure in aggregated form by the end of the seventh daily market session after execution.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: Interruption of an announced buy-back programme across a closed period or a period of delayed disclosure of inside information, where the programme has not been structured as time-scheduled or delegated to an independent lead manager.
proposal.measured_on_intention: German and Dutch regulated-market issuers with a live repurchase authorisation, large- through small-cap bands, restricted to programmes disclosed under the MAR safe harbour and excluding programmes conducted solely to meet employee scheme or convertible obligations.
proposal.mechanism_note: Article 3 of Delegated Regulation 2016/1052 bars the issuer from trading in own shares during a closed period or while it is delaying disclosure of inside information, unless the programme is time-scheduled or is managed by an investment firm taking trading decisions independently of the issuer.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: Publication of a periodic financial report at or near the outer statutory deadline, which simultaneously fixes the end of the associated closed period for managers.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Regulated-market equity issuers in Germany, the Netherlands, France and Belgium, mid- and small-cap bands where reporting calendars are less standardised, excluding issuers on SME growth markets and excluding non-EU issuers reporting under equivalence.
proposal.mechanism_note: Articles 4 and 5 of the Transparency Directive require the annual financial report within four months of the financial year end and the half-yearly report as soon as possible and at the latest three months after the period end. Article 19(11) MAR anchors the closed period to the announcement of the interim or year-end report.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: Composition changes arising from a scheduled index review under a published rulebook, in particular constituents moving through the rulebook's incumbency buffer, where the announcement date and the effective date are separated by a defined interval.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Deutsche Boerse DAX-family and Euronext AEX-family indices, spanning the large-cap through small-cap index tiers, restricted to ordinary share constituents and excluding changes caused by mergers, delistings or trading suspensions.
proposal.mechanism_note: The AEX family rulebook fixes annual and quarterly review cut-off dates, ranks candidates on free float market capitalisation subject to free float velocity or turnover eligibility, and grants incumbents priority inside a defined buffer band before automatic selection or removal applies; announcements precede implementation by a set number of trading days.

labelled.label_note: No issuer, instrument, ticker or dated episode. Names regulators, venues, index families, forms and rule numbers only.

proposal.event_definition: First appearance of a net short position in a national public register, and the symmetric disappearance when a position falls back below the public disclosure threshold while remaining reportable to the regulator.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Shares admitted to trading on Euronext Amsterdam and German regulated markets, mid- and small-cap bands where individual position holders are few, excluding sovereign debt positions and excluding positions held under market-making or primary-dealer exemptions.
proposal.mechanism_note: Under the Short Selling Regulation as applied by the AFM, a net short position must be notified privately to the competent authority at a first threshold and at each further increment, while public disclosure in the national register begins only at a higher threshold and continues at each increment above it.

proposal.event_definition: Ad hoc disclosure of inside information released at the end of a delay period whose stated legitimate interest was a pending public authority approval or an authorisation affecting a product, invention or supply arrangement.
proposal.measured_on_intention: Life-science, medical-technology and diagnostics issuers on Frankfurt Prime Standard and Euronext Amsterdam/Brussels/Paris, mid- and small-cap bands, restricted to issuers whose revenue depends on regulated health-sector authorisations, reimbursement decisions or public tender awards, and excluding diversified industrial conglomerates.
proposal.mechanism_note: Article 17(1) MAR requires disclosure as soon as possible, and Article 17(4) permits delay where legitimate interests are prejudiced, the delay is not likely to mislead the public and confidentiality is maintained, with the competent authority notified afterwards. ESMA's guidelines enumerate legitimate interests that include the issuer having developed a product or invention whose immediate disclosure would jeopardise intellectual property rights.
